summary: The note covers the 2014 United States Senate elections, in which the Republicans regained Senate control for the 114th Congress starting January 2015, after not controlling the Senate since January 2007. Republicans needed a net gain of at least six seats to win a majority, held all of their own seats, and gained nine Democratic-held seats. The excerpt ends as it lists the five Democratic incumbents Republicans defeated.
one_line: The 2014 U.S. Senate elections, in which Republicans regained Senate majority for the 114th Congress starting January 2015.
key_facts: The Republicans regained the majority of the Senate in the 114th Congress, which started in January 2015.
The Republicans had not controlled the Senate since January 2007.
The Republicans needed a net gain of at least six seats to obtain a majority.
The Republicans held all of their seats in the 2014 Senate elections.
The Republicans gained nine Democratic-held seats in the 2014 Senate elections.
Republicans defeated five Democratic incumbents in the 2014 Senate elections.
